artists.biography:
Johnny Marr (born 31 October 1963) is an English musician and songwriter. Marr was co-songwriter – with Morrissey – and guitarist of The Smiths between 1982–87. He also was a member of Electronic, The The and Modest Mouse. In 2008, he joined The Cribs after touring with them on 2008's NME Awards Tour, a group in which he would remain until 2011. In 2012 Marr announced he would be releasing a solo album titled The Messenger.
In 2013, the NME awarded Marr its Godlike Genius award, hailing Marr as "not content with rewriting the history of music with one of the world's greatest ever bands, The Smiths, he's continued to push boundaries and evolve throughout his career, working with some of the best and most exciting artists on the planet." He was voted the fourth best guitarist of the last 30 years in a poll conducted by the BBC in 2010. Phil Alexander, Editor-in-Chief of Mojo, has described Marr as "arguably Britain's last great guitar stylist".

perplexity.description:
Call the Comet" is the third solo studio album by British rock musician Johnny Marr, released on June 15, 2018, through New Voodoo and Warner Bros. Records. Musically, the album blends Britpop, alternative rock, and indie rock, showcasing Marr’s signature guitar work and melodic sensibilities. The record features a cohesive sound built around layered guitars, atmospheric keyboards, and Marr’s distinctive vocals, with themes that touch on dystopia, hope, and resilience. Standout tracks such as "Hi Hello," "The Tracers," and "Spiral Cities" highlight Marr’s ability to craft anthemic, guitar-driven songs while maintaining a sense of introspection and urgency.

As the follow-up to his previous solo efforts, "Call the Comet" solidified Marr’s reputation as a vital solo artist beyond his legendary status as the guitarist for The Smiths. The album received positive reviews, with critics praising its confidence and energy; Clash Music described it as “easily Johnny Marr’s most confident solo album,” rating it 7/10. While not a major commercial blockbuster, the album was well-received by fans and critics alike, affirming Marr’s continued relevance and creative vitality in the rock genre.
